what.t: Polyester yarn, made from crude-oil derivatives, is woven into grey fabric on powerlooms, often as job-work, then dyed, printed, embroidered and finished for dress-material traders and garment buyers.
Surat makes about 65% of India's synthetic textiles, with yearly sales of about Rs 85,000 crore (as cited by the Southern Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry).

money.t: The margin is in processing and finishing; grey fabric is a commodity. Pure job-work units earn only a conversion charge and have no pricing power.
Yarn and power decide the margin. Yarn follows crude oil, so a unit must pass price rises on quickly or absorb them.

checks: Power bills against the shift register, every month: falling machine hours mean a slowdown.
Yarn purchase register against the stock statement, every month: yarn piling up while sales stay flat means the unit is funding inventory instead of selling.
Wage, EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) and ESI (Employees' State Insurance) payments on time: late payments are an early sign of stress or a strike.
Any FIR or labour department notice against the unit.
